newsitem.title: CONGO: French commander joins calls for Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: French commander joins calls for Zaire talks.

text.p: The commander of French troops on stand-by in Congo to evacuate foreigners from Zaire's capital says he hopes African wisdom will prevail and that peace talks will spare Kinshasa a battle that would destroy it.

General Rene Landrin told Reuters that any order to evacuate French and other foreign nationals from Zaire's teeming capital across the Zaire River from Brazzaville would come from Paris on the advice of France's ambassador in Kinshasa.

"I truly hope that we will return home without having to intervene in Kinshasa, that we can count on African wisdom and hope the Zaireans will get together to reach a negotiated settlement," he said in an interview in Congo's capital.
"If the war reaches Kinshasa, the city will be destroyed. No one wants that."

Military sources say that France has 300 soldiers in Congo, Zaire's former colonial ruler Belgium around 500 and the United States around 1,800 -- both in Brazzaville and at sea off Zaire's narrow coastline.
Britain said on Monday it was boosting its contingent in the region to 200.
Laurent Kabila's rebels took up arms in October vowing to topple veteran President Mobutu Sese Seko and now control over half of the sprawling, mineral-rich nation at the heart of Africa.
Rebels advancing on Kinshasa were closing in on the provincial town of Kikwit on Monday and local authorities asked government soldiers to lay down their arms, Kikwit residents said by radio.
U.S. envoy Bill Richardson arrived in Kinshasa on Monday and declared that the United States wanted to see a negotiated settlement in the war.

"The United States believes that there can be no military solution to the crisis, but rather a negotiated settlement leading to an inclusive transitional government and fair and free elections," he said in a prepared arrival statement.
South African and other efforts to broker direct talks between Mobutu and Kabila have foundered on the choice of venue.
Mobutu, who had prostate cancer surgery last August, rejected South Africa on health grounds, Kabila has rejected alternatives such as Brazzaville on security grounds.
Gabon has offered to host the talks. Kabila has suggested Zambia's capital Lusaka.
Landrin said that Western powers had no hidden agenda in Zaire. "We all have the same mission. It is for humanitarian reasons. We must evacuate foreign nationals if the need arises."

He said that the French contingent had been in Congo's capital for six weeks. "All depends on the French ambassador in Kinshasa. It's up to him to advise the people in France, it's up to him to say that conditions require the start of an evacuation."
